function.name: CompositeRuntimeField_createChildRuntimeField
function.description: Attempts to create a child runtime field for a composite field, but since composite fields cannot have children, it throws an IllegalArgumentException. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

parserContext.description: The context used for parsing the mapping. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

parent.description: The name of the parent field. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

parentScriptFactory.description: A factory function to create a script for the parent composite field. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

onScriptError.description: The strategy for handling script errors. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

I tried to invoke the `CompositeRuntimeField_createChildRuntimeField` helper with the parameters you supplied:

```json

  "parserContext": "mappingParserContext",
  "parent": "compositeField1",
  "parentScriptFactory": "compositeScriptFactory",
  "onScriptError": "onScriptError.IGNORE"
}
```

However, this operation fails because **Elasticsearch does not allow composite fields to have child runtime fields**. The underlying implementation throws an `IllegalArgumentException`, indicating that the requested action is unsupported.

In practice, you’ll receive an error similar to:

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Cannot create child runtime field for composite field [compositeField1]
```

Since composite fields cannot contain nested or child fields, you’ll need to rethink your mapping strategy. Some alternatives include:

| Option | What it means | When to use |
|--------|---------------|-------------|
| Add a separate runtime field at the document level | Define a new runtime field that computes values based on existing fields (e.g., concatenating parts of a composite field) | When you need derived data that isn’t part of the original composite structure |
| Use a scripted field in Kibana | Compute values on the fly during query time without storing them | For ad‑hoc calculations that don’t require indexing |
| Store the desired sub‑field separately | Index the sub‑field as its own field (not inside the composite) | When you need to search or aggregate on that sub‑field independently |

If you still want to use a runtime field that depends on the components of `compositeField1`, you can define it at the root level and reference the individual component fields (`compositeField1.part1`, `compositeField1.part2`, etc.) in the script. That way, the runtime field remains independent of the composite field’s internal structure.
